overview: A Pacific system brings snow to the northern Rockies Friday into Saturday, with more mountain snow in the Cascades and Sierra later this week. A stronger storm reaches the Sierra and Wasatch around Monday and Tuesday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A Pacific system arrives late Friday with stronger northwest flow, favoring mountains west of the Divide through Saturday. Winter Storm Warnings cover the western mountains, with snow rates near an inch an hour. Jackson Hole and Grand Targhee are the top bets, with Jackson Hole at 29" and Grand Targhee at 32" for the week. Gusts near 60 mph are possible on the Wind Corridor Friday afternoon.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Freezing rain and rain hit northern New York and Vermont Thursday night into Friday, so expect slick travel and possible outages. Light mountain snow follows over the weekend. A frontal system brings another round of precipitation Sunday night into Monday. Jay Peak has the most snow of the Northeast resorts at 30" for the week.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Atmospheric river rain falls through Friday, with mountain snow above 4000 to 5500 feet and a Winter Weather Advisory likely for the pass areas. Snow levels stay high for the Oregon Blues, so expect mostly rain there. A more active pattern returns early next week. Mt. Bachelor leads at 26" for the week.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Saturday, with fog possible in the valleys. A wet system arrives Sunday into Monday, bringing light snow above 7500 feet and thunderstorm chances. Snow levels then rise above 8000 feet. Kirkwood leads the area at 25" for the week, with the heaviest snow expected Monday night into Tuesday.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mild and dry through Saturday. Rain and high-elevation snow return Sunday into Tuesday, with strong ridgetop winds gusting 60 to 80 mph Sunday night into Monday. The NWS is calling for more, 22 to 37 inches Sunday night through Tuesday night. Mammoth leads at 21" for the week, with the storm arriving late Monday night into Tuesday.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Dry through Friday, with a weak storm bringing mountain snow to northern Utah Friday night into Saturday. Dry weather returns Sunday, then a stronger storm arrives around Tuesday. Alta and Snowbird lead at about 21" each for the week, with most of the total coming Tuesday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Showers and rain dominate Friday and through early next week, with snow levels too high for most of the terrain. Mixed rain and snow returns Monday before a cooler period. Cypress Mountain leads at 24" for the week, with the bulk arriving Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A fast shortwave brings snow to the northern and central Colorado mountains from Friday night into Saturday, with gusts of 45 to 60 mph above treeline. Winter Weather Advisories cover the Park, Elkhead, Flat Tops and Central mountains. The Park Range sees the least. Steamboat leads at 22" for the week, with Saturday the big day.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mostly mixed sun and cloud through Saturday, then rain or snow from Sunday night into Monday. Whitewater leads at 12" for the week, with Monday the biggest day.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Snow arrives Sunday night, mixing with rain Monday. Expect light totals, with SilverStar leading at 7" for the week and Sun Peaks close behind.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
